messages.content: How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?

function.name: thermodynamics_calc_gas_pressure
function.description: Calculate gas pressure in a closed chamber due to heating Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

volume.description: The volume of the chamber in cubic meters. This is a float type value.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

initial_pressure.description: The initial pressure of the gas in Pascal. Default is standard atmospheric pressure. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?" They want to know how much gas is generated. But the chamber is closed, so no gas is generated; the amount of gas remains constant. The question might be about expansion or pressure change. The user might be confused. We can explain that the amount of gas (moles) remains constant; only pressure changes. We can calculate the new pressure using ideal gas law: P2 = P1 * T2/T1. T in Kelvin. So T1=298K, T2=373K. So P2 = 101325 Pa * 373/298 ≈ 126,700 Pa. So pressure increases. The volume remains constant. So no gas is generated. We can also mention that the amount of gas is constant. So answer: no gas generated; pressure increases. Provide calculation.
